chunks: Musa ibn al-Qasim from Hammad ibn Isa from Umar ibn Udhaynah from Zurarah ibn A'yan said:
I asked Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him): 'Which is superior in merit, Hajj or Umrah?' He said: 'The Umrah al-Mufradah (independent Umrah), then he goes wherever he wishes.'
And he said: 'Umrah is obligatory upon the creation, in the status of Hajj, because Allah the Exalted says:
And complete the Hajj and Umrah for Allah
And indeed, the ruling of Umrah was revealed in Medina, so the best Umrah is the Umrah of Rajab.
And he said: 'The one who performs Umrah al-Mufradah, if he performs Umrah in Rajab then stays in Mecca until Hajj, his Umrah is complete and his Hajj is incomplete (Meccan).'
And whoever 'enjoys Umrah until Hajj' (Umrat al-Tamattu'), the obligation of Umrah falls from him. Narrated.

key_terms.الْعُمْرَةُ الْمُفْرَدَةُ: Independent Umrah (Umrah performed separately from Hajj)
key_terms.مَكِّيَّةً: Meccan (referring to the location/status of the ritual)

ai.seo_question: What is the difference between Umrah al-Mufradah and Umrat al-Tamattu' in Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) establishes the obligatory nature of Umrah by citing the Quranic command to complete both Hajj and Umrah for Allah, a verse revealed in Medina. He provides detailed jurisprudential distinctions between Umrah al-Mufradah and Umrat al-Tamattu', highlighting the superior merit of performing Umrah in the sacred month of Rajab. This narration underscores the Shia view that while Umrah is a distinct pillar, its performance can be integrated with Hajj to fulfill religious obligations efficiently.
